subject: DPA & SCCs: connector review and risk resolution (Order Form)
messages:
From: Sara Griffin <sara@lifecast.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@lifecast.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA & SCCs: connector review and risk resolution (Order Form)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the connector flow looked good. Legal at Lifecast ran a quick pass on the draft Order Form + DPA and came back with a short list of sticking points they want us to prioritize before procurement can issue a PO. See attachments (annotated SCCs + our proposed redline). High level asks from their side: 

- Clear role mapping for the connector (controller v. processor for telemetry and support logs).
- Confirmation of KMS usage and SSAE/SOC evidence for key management.
- A transfer mitigation appendix for EU -> US control plane access; they asked for additional contractual language beyond SCCs.
- Limitation of liability carveouts tied to data residency failures.

Can you and your legal partner run a 30–40 minute risk-resolution call today? Tom (cc'd) is the procurement lead and would like the conversation to also cover the sequencing/timeline for a signed Order Form. If you can't do today, earliest tomorrow EMEA morning works.

Thanks — attaching the two files we referenced.

Sara
Sara Griffin
Head of Procurement, Lifecast Health
--
Attachments: Lifecast_SCCs_annotated.pdf (pdf), proposed-dpa-redline.docx (docx)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Griffin <sara@lifecast.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA & SCCs: connector review and risk resolution (Order Form)

Sara — thanks for sending this through and for the clear bulleted asks. We're available for a short call today at 14:00 CEST (13:00 UK). I've looped in Ben (privacy counsel) and Laura (licensing/order form PM) so we can cover both legal and procurement sequencing.

Quick notes before the call so we can be efficient: 
1) Role mapping: Our standard position is that Redwood acts as processor for customer data, but connector telemetry (error traces & ingestion logs) is scoped as operation-only telemetry — we'll propose explicit exclusions in the DPA exhibit to avoid ambiguity.
2) KMS: Redwood supports CMKs via customer-managed KMS on Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we offer application-level encryption + strict key custodianship. We can provide SOC2 Type II + KMS configuration snapshot — Ben will confirm evidence availability on the call.
3) Transfer mitigation: We prefer relying on SCCs + technical mitigations (encryption-in-transit, region pinning), but we can offer an additional contractual appendix with a commitments table (who does what, escalation contact, targeted timelines for data localization remediation) — scope and SLA will affect pricing.
4) Liability carveouts: we will need to review Lifecast's proposed language line-by-line; this typically drives legal escalation and potentially commercial offset.

Call invite sent separately. If you can reply with the top 3 clauses in your redline you expect resolution on today, we can prioritize prep.

Best,
Markus
VP Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Griffin <sara@lifecast.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA & SCCs: connector review and risk resolution (Order Form)

Sara / team — appreciate the packet. I pulled a quick read of the proposed redline and flagged three priority items I think we can move on in the call: 

- Role clarity for connector telemetry (propose explicit Exhibit B language: "Connector telemetry is operational telemetry, collected only for ingestion/diagnostics and is not used for model retraining or profiling without Customer consent").
- KMS evidence: we can provide SOC2 + proof-of-configuration screenshots for hosted KMS parameters; for Dedicated/Private we can commit to customer-managed keys.
- Transfer appendix: we can offer a Transfer Mitigation Annex (TMA) that maps controls, corrective actions and a 30/60/90 remediation runway in the rare event of residency breach; important: specific SLOs in the annex will be billable if they require Dedicated/Private changes.

I recommend we do not agree to broad liability carveouts tied to data residency failure without a proportional cap; propose we recommend a compromise: a narrowly scoped warranty for data residency with a capped remedy (credits + remediation assistance).

Neha — can you surface any recent similar language we used for the Aurelius order? I'm happy to quote that as precedent on the call.

Ben
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Griffin <sara@lifecast.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@lifecast.com>, Lifecast Legal <legal@lifecast.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA & SCCs: connector review and risk resolution (Order Form)

Thanks — that sounds constructive. Top 3 clauses Lifecast wants resolved today: 

1) Residency warranty + remedies (we want a stronger contractual commitment around timely remediation if data moves outside agreed regions).
2) SCCs: Lifecast counsel included a small deviation in the SCCs around subprocessor onboarding notice (they want 30 days notice and right to object rather than 15).
3) Role mapping for connector telemetry (as Ben captured).

Tom and our legal team will be on the call; priority is to lock the Order Form timeline so procurement can circulate a PO by EOW, subject to legal signoff. If the Transfer Mitigation Annex will add cost, call that out — procurement needs to know.

Looking forward,
Sara
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Lifecast call follow-up items

Internal notes from today's call (action items / suggested positions):

- Offer a Transfer Mitigation Annex (TMA) with three risk tiers: 
  * Tier 1 (configurable via order form) — region pinning + log-access controls (no extra charge).
  * Tier 2 (operational commitment) — 30/60/90 remediation runway + named escalation contacts (may incur small setup fee).
  * Tier 3 (dedicated deployment fallback) — Dedicated or Private deployment option (commercial commit required).

- SCCs / Subprocessor notice: counter-propose 21-day notice with a formal objection right for material processors; provide an expedited exception path for critical security patches.

- Residency warranty: do not accept an open-ended warranty. Propose a narrow warranty tied to our region pinning controls and offer a capped credit-based remedy plus remediation assistance.

- Evidence pack: Laura to drop SOC2 extract & KMS screenshots into the Drive link by EOD. Neha to surface precedent clause (Aurelius LF-2026-004) for liability cap language. Ben to prepare a short redline of the proposed-dpa-redline.docx highlighting the three agreed positions for tomorrow's legal handoff.

I'll prep the proposed TMA template and circulate a short note to Lifecast legal tomorrow AM.

Markus
VP Partnerships, Redwood Inference
